newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shanghai Ind placement well received.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Ind placement well received.

text.p: The share placement of Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, the Hong Kong-listed arm of the Shanghai municipal government, has been warmly received by the market, chairman Cai Lai Xing said.

"The market's reception of the placement is very good," he told a news conference adding that Monday's active share trading and rise in share price was to be expected following the company's weekend news of substantial asset injections.
Shanghai Industrial shares rose HK$1.65, or 7.78 percent, on Monday to HK$22.85 on volume of 13.27 million shares.

The company said it would issue 162 million new shares to Shanghai Investment Holdings Ltd (SIH), its immediate holding company, at HK$19.50 per share to fund the purchase of various automotive, infrastructure, food and commercial interests for an aggregate HK$2.7 billion.
Cai said the asset purchases fulfilled promises made by the company in its listing document and were in line with the firm's development direction.

"We had promised when we listed that after asset injections, earnings per share would not be diluted but increased to secure shareholders' interests. Our earnings per share was HK$0.579 and after asset injections will be HK$0.79," Cai said.
Cai did not specify which reporting period he was refering to. Shanghai Industrial reported consolidated earnings per share for the first half of the year of HK$0.58 per share.
Cai also said he hoped Shanghai Industrial's share price would not rise too high, too fast. "What we are looking for is a steady and solid development," he added.
Shanghai Industrial was listed in Hong Kong on May 30 at HK$7.28 per share.
